howto.name: Enter a HEX color
howto.text: Type a 6-digit code such as #FF5733, or a 3-digit short form such as #369, into the Hex box; capitals and lower case both work. The page opens on #0E8A56. Spaces, alpha digits and color names such as red are not accepted and show Invalid hex color.

howto.name: Or pick from the swatch
howto.text: Click the large swatch marked Click to edit to open your browser's color picker; the color you choose replaces the Hex value.

howto.name: Read every format
howto.text: The R, G and B values appear under the Hex box. Below, the All formats list has six rows: HEX (your code in capitals), RGB, RGBA with an alpha of 1, HSL rounded to whole numbers, a Tailwind arbitrary-value class and a CSS custom property named --brand.

howto.name: Check the contrast badge
howto.text: The badge on the swatch rates your color against white and black text with the WCAG 2.x contrast formula and shows the higher ratio to one decimal place. A black badge means black text reads better on the color; a white badge means white text does.

howto.name: Copy the value you need
howto.text: Each row has its own Copy button, which copies exactly the text shown, such as rgb(14, 138, 86) or --brand: #0e8a56;. If the browser blocks clipboard access, a message asks you to select the value and copy it manually.

faq.q: What does the starting color #0E8A56 convert to?
faq.a: R 14, G 138, B 86, shown as rgb(14, 138, 86) and rgba(14, 138, 86, 1). HSL is hsl(155, 82%, 30%), the Tailwind row is bg-[#0e8a56] and the CSS variable row is --brand: #0e8a56;. The badge is black and reads AA · 4.8:1, because the contrast is 4.79:1 against black and 4.39:1 against white.

faq.q: What happens with a 3-digit code like #369?
faq.a: Each digit is doubled, so #369 is read as #336699: rgb(51, 102, 153) and hsl(210, 50%, 40%), with a white AA · 6.0:1 badge. The HEX, Tailwind and CSS variable rows keep the short code as typed (#369, bg-[#369] and --brand: #369;), which is still valid CSS.
No. Input is a 3- or 6-digit HEX code without alpha, so a 4- or 8-digit code such as #FF5733CC shows Invalid hex color, and the RGBA row always ends with an alpha of 1.

faq.q: What does the contrast badge mean?
faq.a: It applies the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula to compare your color with pure white and pure black, keeps the higher ratio and rates it AAA at 7:1 or more, AA at 4.5:1 or more, AA Large at 3:1 or more and Fail below 3:1. Since black or white always reaches at least 4.58:1 against any color, a valid code always rates AA or AAA: the badge tells you which text color to use, not whether two of your own colors contrast.

faq.q: Why does the badge show Fail · 1.0:1?
faq.a: Only while the Hex box holds an invalid code, such as one with a missing digit or a stray space; the All formats list is then replaced by Invalid hex color. Correct the code and both update.

faq.q: Why does a 7.0:1 ratio show AA, not AAA?
faq.a: The ratio is rounded to one decimal place for display, but the rating uses the exact value. #0038FF, for example, has a contrast of 6.98:1 against white, so its badge reads AA · 7.0:1.

faq.q: Can I type RGB, HSL or a color name?
faq.a: No. The only inputs are the Hex box and the color picker; the other formats are outputs. Type the # too: without it the RGB and HSL rows still work, but the HEX, Tailwind and CSS variable rows repeat the code without a # (for example bg-[0e8a56]), which CSS does not accept, and the swatch keeps its previous color.
Yes. The conversions and contrast math run in JavaScript on this page, and the tool makes no network request, so the colors you try are not sent to PrivaTools.
